sources.single: agent.predict(state, {qid: qdef}) called once per item, wall-clock time.time() around the call
sources.batched: agent.prepare() per item -> laya_mlx.agent.collate_items() -> agent.forward(), batch_size=agent.batch_size (16); system_one/predict only batches multiple QUESTIONS on one shared state, so cross-item batching reuses the package's own lower primitives

critic_notes.batched_p50_p99_are_amortized: run_zeroshot.py records batch_wall/len(chunk) for every item in a batch, so batched p50_ms/p99_ms are amortized cost per item, not the latency an item sees; an item in a 16-item batch waits the whole batch wall (~16 x 38.5 = ~616 ms at the p50 batch)
critic_notes.note: RSS (~935 MiB) understates the process's memory cost; macOS peak memory footprint was ~11.3 GiB on a 16 GiB host. What makes up the footprint (e.g. MLX/Metal buffers) was not verified.
